Incident: Evasive Panda MgBot backdoor delivered through Tencent QQ update channel
Access path: Trojanized QQ Windows updater (QQUrlMgr.exe) fetched the MgBot installer from a hardcoded update.browser.qq[.]com URL. ESET could not determine whether Tencent's update servers were compromised or an adversary-in-the-middle attack (e.g. via routers or ISP infrastructure) was used.
Orgs reached (as reported): No total reported. ESET (Apr 2023) lists victims in Gansu, Guangdong and Jiangsu provinces, China, from 2020 to 2021. Most belong to one international NGO, plus one victim in Nigeria.
Coding notes: Delivery method unresolved: ESET calls the supply-chain hypothesis speculation and cannot rule out an AitM attack. ESET says only MgBot was observed on victim machines and does not mention lateral movement. Execute commands is NR because the commands run (net start AppMgmt, rundll32) are installer design, not operator activity. Crossed customer boundary is NR because ESET does not say any provider held customer data.

Incident: Independent Living Systems (ILS) breach
Access path: Unauthorized actor accessed ILS's network 30 Jun-5 Jul 2022 and acquired files holding data of ILS's managed-care clients (initial vector not reported)
Orgs reached (as reported): Not stated as a count of client organisations. ILS's own subsidiaries (Florida Community Care LLC; HPMP of Florida Inc dba Florida Complete Care) plus other unnamed data-owner clients and health plans. Telligen (an Iowa Medicaid contractor) is a named downstream client. Up to 4,226,508 individuals were reported by ILS to the Maine AG.
Coding notes: I could not read the PDF text; the HIPAA Journal summary of the ILS notice and Maine AG filing supplied the facts, so primary-source verification is partial. Systems became inaccessible on 5 Jul 2022, which suggests ransomware, but the notice does not say so, so Ransomware is NR. Exfiltration is coded Y because ILS says files were acquired. ILS is a TPA, not an IT provider, so I coded it General supply-chain.
People or orgs exposed: 4,226,508 individuals (ILS filing with Maine AG, notices mailed from 14 Mar 2023; the initial HHS entry was a 501 placeholder)

Incident: Aesto Health AWS environment breach
Access path: Unauthorized third party accessed part of Aesto's AWS infrastructure (about 2-18 December 2025), which held patient data of its healthcare-provider clients. The initial access method was not reported.
Orgs reached (as reported): Roughly 29-39 healthcare provider clients, as listed by HIPAA Journal (secondary, Sept 2026). Aesto's primary notice and HHS filing report individuals (9,540,683), not a client count.
Coding notes: I read the Aesto notice and HHS filing only through BleepingComputer and HIPAA Journal. I could not extract the AG PDFs. Data 'may have been accessed and/or acquired', so exfiltration is NR. Client count is secondary and varies (29 vs 39). Intrusion 2-18 Dec 2025; first public notice 24 Jun 2026. No techniques, ransomware or outage were reported.

Incident: Episource (medical coding and risk-adjustment vendor, Optum subsidiary) breach
Access path: Intruder gained unauthorized access to Episource's own systems (initial vector not disclosed) from 27 Jan to 6 Feb 2025. Episource then held data for its health-plan and provider clients, and that data was copied. Clients were affected through the vendor's data holdings.
Orgs reached (as reported): Episource notices say not all customers were affected. Named clients: Sharp HealthCare (24,971 individuals), Sharp Community Medical Group (2,029), Wellcare, Anthem/Wellpoint and VNS Health plans. The total number of client organisations is not reported.
Coding notes: I could not read the notice PDF text, so I relied on secondary summaries of the notices and the HHS filing for the details below. Episource does not confirm ransomware. A client (Sharp) called it ransomware, so I coded Ransomware as NR. Counts: 5,418,866 initially (HHS, June 2025); a revised 6,725,572 is reported secondarily. Exfiltration is confirmed.
People or orgs exposed: 5,418,866 individuals (HHS OCR filing, June 2025). A later revised figure of 6,725,572 is reported by HIPAA Journal from updated OCR data; I could not verify it against the portal.

Incident: Rspack npm packages (@rspack/core, @rspack/cli 1.1.7) compromised
Access path: Attacker obtained a token for a team member with Rspack org permissions (maintainers say it was stolen via a 'Pwn request' on public GitHub Actions in another organization) and published malicious 1.1.7 of @rspack/core and @rspack/cli to npm; the postinstall script ran on install.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown; no confirmed count of affected installs. Socket reported about 370K weekly downloads of @rspack/core and about 135K of @rspack/cli, which is exposure rather than confirmed victims.
Coding notes: The only primary source found is the maintainers' GitHub issue, which covers cause, versions and response but not payload behaviour. Payload details (XMRig download to /tmp/vant_helper, IP lookup, fetch from 80.78.28.72/tokens) come from Socket, a secondary source. Exfiltration is unconfirmed. No MSP link, so General supply-chain.

Incident: Elgon Information Systems ransomware breach (2023; HHS OCR settlement Jan 2025)
Access path: Unknown actor reached an Elgon server through open firewall ports on 25 Mar 2023; Elgon found a ransom note on 31 Mar 2023. Elgon is an EMR and billing-support provider that held data for HIPAA covered entities (OCR press release as relayed by HIPAA Journal and The Record).
Orgs reached (as reported): Number of covered-entity customers not reported. 31,248 individuals affected, per Elgon's June 2023 HHS breach report (via OCR).
Coding notes: HHS pages returned 403, so I could not read them. Facts come from news that relays the OCR release (HIPAA Journal, The Record). The ransom note is the only reported ransomware evidence. No source states encryption or exfiltration. Multiple customers are inferred from the provider's role. Year is the first disclosure to HHS (June 2023) or the OCR settlement (Jan 2025); I used 2025.
People or orgs exposed: 31,248 individuals (HHS breach report, June 2023; OCR settlement Jan 2025)

Incident: MOVEit Transfer mass exploitation (CVE-2023-34362, Cl0p), May-June 2023
Access path: Cl0p exploited SQL injection zero-day CVE-2023-34362 in internet-facing MOVEit Transfer servers, including MOVEit Cloud and servers run by service providers holding client data. They installed the LEMURLOOT web shell (human2.aspx) and pulled files from the MOVEit databases.
Orgs reached (as reported): Hundreds. CISA/FBI advisory AA23-158A (June 2023) described widespread exploitation, and Cl0p listed hundreds of victims on its leak site. Emsisoft's tracker (non-primary) counts about 2,700 orgs and about 95M individuals.
Coding notes: Compiled from memory of the cited sources without re-opening them, so figures and quotes are unchecked. Deployed the LEMURLOOT web shell, so Deploy software and Software deployment are Y and the tier is 3. Azure credential theft and account creation are web-shell design features, not observed, so NR. CISA described data theft and extortion, with no encryption, so Ransomware is N. Provider relevance rests on providers whose MOVEit servers held many clients' data. Counts vary by source.
People or orgs exposed: About 2,700 orgs and about 95M individuals (Emsisoft tracker, non-primary, 2024). Primary figures are fragmentary: CISA/FBI describe 'hundreds', and state breach notifications are filed per organisation.

Incident: React Native ARIA / gluestack-ui npm package compromise
Access path: A leaked npm access token belonging to an authorised maintainer, with no 2FA, was used to publish trojanised versions of 16 @react-native-aria packages and @gluestack-ui/core (the same code appears under @gluestack-ui/utils in Aikido's report). The versions carried an obfuscated remote access trojan that contacted a C2 server.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. No victim count was reported. About 1.02 million combined weekly downloads (Gluestack, 17 packages) is exposure, not confirmed infections. Aikido gave about 1.05 million.
Coding notes: No MSP involvement, so General supply-chain. The command execution and file upload described in the Aikido analysis come from the malware's design, not observed use, so behaviours are NR and only capabilities are Y. Gluestack reports no evidence of exfiltration and no confirmed system compromise. Package count differs between sources (16 or 17). Gluestack's report gives the first compromise as 6 June 2025 and public disclosure as 9 June. Year is taken from that.

Incident: XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094)
Access path: A maintainer identity (Jia Tan) gained commit and release rights to the upstream xz project over about two years. Trojanised release tarballs for 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 carried a build-time script that injected a backdoor into liblzma. Distributions that linked sshd to liblzma (via systemd) shipped it.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. No confirmed victims or exploitation were reported. The affected versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 were found mainly in development and testing distributions (Fedora Rawhide/40 beta, Debian testing/unstable, Kali, openSUSE Tumbleweed). Reported by Openwall/Andres Freund, CISA and NVD.
Coding notes: Sources not fetched in this session; coded from the advisories as recalled. Execute commands is the capability as described in the CVE (pre-auth remote command execution via sshd for a holder of a specific key); it was not observed. All behaviours are NR because no exploitation was reported. Reach is Unknown. No MSP involvement; trust boundary could also be read as Build or release pipeline.

Incident: Renkim Corporation
Access path: Unauthorized access to Renkim's internal network (initial vector not disclosed), reaching client-provided mailing files that Renkim held for healthcare clients
Orgs reached (as reported): Unconfirmed total. Named clients: Ballard Health, NYC Health + Hospitals (5,728 patients, per its notice), Wakefield and Associates. 46,592 individuals in total (HIPAA Journal, from the HHS filing); 46,864 in the Maine AG filing
Coding notes: Renkim is a print/mail vendor, not an IT or hosting provider, so General supply-chain. The regulator pages returned 403, so the details come from the NYC H+H notice and HIPAA Journal's reading of the filings. Exfiltration is reported only as 'likely' (secondary), so NR. Unauthorized access ran March 2-3, 2025. First public notice was June 2025; the NYC H+H notice is dated June 6.
People or orgs exposed: 46,592 individuals (HHS breach filing per HIPAA Journal, mid-2025); 46,864 in the Maine AG filing; 5,728 NYC H+H patients (June 2025)

Incident: Kong Ingress Controller 3.4.0 official image compromised (December 2024; post-mortem January 2025)
Access path: Attacker opened a pull request from a fork against an old Kong branch that still had a vulnerable pull_request_target workflow. They used the Cacheract tool to take build-pipeline secrets, including a GitHub personal access token. With that token they triggered protected workflows, deleted the workflow logs, and pushed a cryptominer-laden image to Kong's official DockerHub repository under the :latest, :3.4 and :3.4.0 tags.
Orgs reached (as reported): Image downloaded 202 times (Kong, post-mortem). Kong says a relatively small number of users were affected and gives no count of affected customers.
Coding notes: No MSP involvement, so General supply-chain. The path was a GitHub Actions pipeline compromise, not a leaked DockerHub token, which some news reports claimed. The 202 downloads count is not a count of orgs. 'Read data' is Y only because the attacker took pipeline secrets, and Kong reports no exfiltration of customer data. I did not open the GitHub advisory directly; its URL comes from search results.

Incident: Shai-Hulud self-propagating npm worm (first wave)
Access path: Malicious versions of npm packages (starting with @ctrl/tinycolor), published with stolen maintainer npm tokens, ran a post-install bash script on developer and CI machines. The script scanned for secrets (TruffleHog), exfiltrated them to an attacker endpoint and to a public GitHub repo named Shai-Hulud, then used stolen npm tokens to republish other packages the maintainer owned.
Orgs reached (as reported): More than 500 npm packages compromised (CISA alert, 23 Sep 2025). The number of downstream organisations was not reported.
Coding notes: No MSP involvement reported, so General supply-chain. The CISA alert does not name TruffleHog, and Unit 42 does not state the number of victim orgs. Package counts vary by source (more than 500 is the most consistent). Software deployment means self-publishing to npm. Unit 42 reports SSH keys only as a lateral-movement risk, so Lateral movement is NR. GitHub Actions persistence belongs to the November 2.0 wave, not this one.
People or orgs exposed: NR (more than 500 packages compromised, CISA, 23 Sep 2025; no figure for orgs or people)

Incident: ctx PyPI package takeover via expired maintainer email domain
Access path: The attacker re-registered the expired domain behind the maintainer's PyPI email address on 14 May 2022 and completed a password reset about 12 minutes later. They deleted the original ctx releases and uploaded malicious versions.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. PyPI reported no victim count. Press cited about 22,000 weekly downloads, which is not a count of compromised installs.
Coding notes: No MSP involvement, so General supply-chain. Boundary could also be Plugin, extension or package; I chose the hijacked maintainer account. The ISC diary (analyst report) describes the code taking AWS keys or all environment variables, Base64-encoded and sent to an attacker Heroku app. I could not open the PSF full incident report. Impact count NR.

Incident: Accellion File Transfer Appliance (FTA) zero-day exploitation campaign (Dec 2020 to early 2021)
Access path: Unauthenticated exploitation of four zero-day flaws in internet-facing legacy Accellion FTA appliances (SQL injection, OS command execution, SSRF). The attackers used them to install the DEWMODE web shell, list files and download them.
Orgs reached (as reported): No count in CISA or Mandiant reports. Accellion stated fewer than 100 of about 300 FTA customers were affected, with about 25 having significant data theft (vendor statement, Feb 2021; not fetched directly).
Coding notes: FTA was a vendor appliance hosted by each customer, not a provider-hosted service. No trust-boundary option fits well, so 'Service provider holding customer data' is the closest. Crossed boundary is NR because victims' own data was taken. Mandiant says no lateral movement was seen and no ransomware was used in the extortion cases. A gzip archive (cache.js.gz) was inferred, not confirmed, so Archive creation is NR. The Accellion count was not checked at source.

Incident: @lottiefiles/lottie-player npm package compromise
Access path: Attacker used a compromised npm access token or account of a LottieFiles developer (LottieFiles later described it as phishing-driven account takeover) to publish malicious versions 2.0.5-2.0.7 directly to npm, bypassing the GitHub release process. Sites loading @latest via CDNs served the malicious code to visitors.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown; no count reported. LottieFiles described 'a large number of users' served via CDNs; package has more than 90,000 downloads (LottieFiles) and 94,000 weekly (Sonatype).
Coding notes: Not an MSP incident; coded General supply-chain. LottieFiles says customer data, platform and repos were not compromised, so Crossed customer boundary is N. Cause is described as token compromise and as phishing takeover. Victim loss (10 BTC) is unconfirmed, from vendor/news. The GitHub link is a placeholder, not verified as the disclosure; the LottieFiles post is the only primary source I read.

Incident: ApolloMD Business Services
Access path: Unauthorized third party accessed ApolloMD's network (initial vector not disclosed) on May 22-23, 2025; ApolloMD is a physician practice management/business services provider holding patient data for 11 covered-entity practice clients; Qilin ransomware group claimed it
Orgs reached (as reported): 11 covered-entity physician practice clients (ApolloMD notices, via HIPAA Journal); 626,540 individuals per HHS OCR (Feb 2, 2026)
Coding notes: Primary source is ApolloMD's own notice, reproduced on class-action sites; I could not fetch it directly and relied on search summaries, HIPAA Journal and the HHS OCR figure. Reach band should be Several to Dozens: 11 practices is Dozens. Encryption was not confirmed by ApolloMD; Qilin's claim is unverified, so ransomware is NR. No techniques reported.

Incident: 3CX DesktopApp trojanized build
Access path: North Korea-linked UNC4736 first compromised 3CX through a trojanized X_TRADER installer. It then used FRP, a reverse proxy, to move laterally and harvest credentials, and reached the Windows and macOS build servers. It trojanized the signed 3CX DesktopApp (18.12.407/416 and macOS builds), which customers received as a normal update. The app loaded SUDDENICON, which fetched C2 addresses from encrypted icon files on GitHub and then downloaded ICONICSTEALER.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. Mandiant reported no victim count. 3CX's customer base is a separate figure and is not a count of affected organisations, so the exact number is NR.
Coding notes: Relevance is MSP-relevant because 3CX is a VoIP/PBX vendor and not itself an MSP. Lateral movement and credential theft were observed inside 3CX's own environment, not at customers. Shellcode execution and command running are observed malware functions. Persistence via the IKEEXT service was reported for the TAXHAUL launcher. No customer count was found in the sources read; the 3CX Mandiant and community pages could not be fetched.

Incident: Comm100 Live Chat desktop installer trojanized (September 2022)
Access path: Attackers replaced the signed Comm100 Live Chat desktop installer on the vendor's website (27-29 Sept 2022). The installer carried a JavaScript backdoor in main.js. It fetched a second-stage script, then a DLL side-loading loader that injected a payload into notepad.exe.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown number; CrowdStrike reported victims in industrial, healthcare, technology, manufacturing, insurance and telecommunications sectors in North America and Europe, with no count given
Coding notes: Only one primary source, the CrowdStrike blog. Comm100 is a chat vendor, not an MSP, so I coded it MSP-relevant. The blog gives no victim count. The second stage spawned cmd.exe, so I coded Shell as Y. It did not mention PowerShell, credential theft, persistence or exfiltration. I did not find an explicit statement that no customer data was exposed, so the customer-boundary field stays N by convention. Reconsider that field.

Incident: Oracle Health (Cerner) legacy data-migration servers breach
Access path: Attacker used stolen customer credentials to log in to legacy Cerner servers that had not yet been migrated to Oracle Cloud and copied data to a remote server. Oracle, as hosting/data-migration provider, held hospital customers' patient data. Access window 22 Jan to 1 Apr 2025.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown number of hospital/healthcare customers; Oracle gave no count. Texas AG portal (2 Oct 2026) lists 2,992,244 Texans; Bloomberg/SecurityWeek tally nearly 19.9 million patients nationwide.
Primary source: https://oag.my.site.com/datasecuritybreachreport/apex/DataSecurityReportsPage (Texas AG breach portal, Cerner entry, 2 Oct 2026) ; https://health.adventhealth.com/oracle-health-data-incident (hospital customer notice relaying Oracle notice)
Coding notes: Primary sources not read directly: AdventHealth page returned 403 and the Texas portal was not fetched. Details come from SecurityWeek's summary of Oracle's customer notice and state filings. Oracle's wording was 'may' have included patient data. Credential theft is the entry method, but credential access is NR as an attacker behaviour. Extortion was reported, with no encryption.
People or orgs exposed: About 19.9 million individuals (Texas AG portal as reported by Bloomberg/SecurityWeek, Oct 2026); Texas 2,992,244; Oracle has not confirmed

Incident: Integrated Oncology Network (ION) phishing-related breach of employee email and SharePoint accounts
Access path: Phishing of a small number of ION employee email and SharePoint accounts (13-16 Dec 2024). ION is a management services organisation holding patient data for its affiliated oncology practices.
Orgs reached (as reported): About 26 affiliated oncology practices and imaging centres reported to HHS OCR or state regulators, per HIPAA Journal's tally of regulator filings (July 2025). Not confirmed in ION's own notice.
Primary source: https://www.ionetwork.com/notice-of-email-phishing-incident (redirects to navista.com; not read directly) ; https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/breach/breach_report.jsf (not directly read; per HIPAA Journal summary)
Coding notes: Primary notices were not directly readable, so the facts come from secondary summaries of ION's notice and regulator filings. 'Ransomware' is N because ION said the likely purpose was a follow-on phishing scheme. Figures conflict: 117,406 (HIPAA Journal), 122,950 (ClaimDepot). I coded 'Exfiltration' NR because the notice says the accounts were only 'accessed'.
People or orgs exposed: About 117,000 to 123,000 individuals across about 26 entities (secondary tallies, July 2025 and later). ION did not disclose its own count.

Incident: Ultralytics YOLO PyPI package versions 8.3.41-8.3.46 compromised via GitHub Actions (December 2024)
Access path: Attacker injected code through a malicious branch name into the pull_request_target trigger of the format.yml GitHub Actions workflow. That gave access to the privileged runner, where the attacker took the repository's PyPI API token. Malicious releases 8.3.41 and 8.3.42 were built through the workflow, which the PyPI blog says targeted the GitHub Actions cache. Releases 8.3.45 and 8.3.46 were published with the stolen token.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. The primary sources give no install or download counts. PyPI reported that versions 8.3.41, 8.3.42, 8.3.45 and 8.3.46 were removed.
Coding notes: No MSP is involved, so I coded this as general supply-chain. I took the build pipeline as the trust boundary, because the compromise began in GitHub Actions. The Package alternative is defensible. The miner payload is described only in the issue thread. Credential access is the runner secret and PyPI token theft. The sources do not give victim counts. Ransomware is N because the payload was a cryptominer.

Incident: TGI Direct (printing/mailing vendor) MOVEit Transfer breach
Access path: Unauthorised access to TGI's own MOVEit Transfer server (managed file transfer tool), where unusual activity was observed on 28 May 2023. The MOVEit vulnerability is not named in the notice I could read. TGI held customer files for its printing and mailing work. Notice was filed in January 2024.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. TGI's notice to the Maryland AG (18 Jan 2024) is on behalf of its client organisations, and the number is not given in what I could read. The Washington AG listing reportedly shows 3,428 Washington residents, but I could only see this through an aggregator.
Coding notes: The Maryland PDF returned 403 on fetch, so details come from search-result excerpts of it. TGI is a printing/mailing vendor, not an IT or hosting provider, so I coded it General supply-chain. The notice says data "could have been subject to" access, so Read data is Y with that caveat. The number of client organisations is not reported. I found no other primary source.
People or orgs exposed: NR for the total. The Washington listing reportedly shows 3,428 residents (secondary source, January 2024).

Incident: CareCloud AWS-hosted EHR environment breach
Access path: Unauthorized third party accessed the AWS environment hosting one of CareCloud's six EHR environments (CareCloud Health) between March 10 and 16, 2026. The initial access method was not disclosed.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown. CareCloud (8-K, March 2026) said one of six EHR environments was affected and has not named the affected provider clients. It serves over 45,000 providers (HIPAA Journal, August 2026).
Coding notes: I could not open the EDGAR 8-K directly (accession 0001493152-26-013239), so the 8-K text comes from a mirror and the later facts from HIPAA Journal, which cites the HHS portal and state AG notices. The 8-K date is reported as March 27, with March 24 as the materiality date. The 3,756,469 figure is from the HHS portal as reported by HIPAA Journal. Exfiltration rests on the actor's claim and the later notifications. No technique details are given.
People or orgs exposed: 3,756,469 individuals on the HHS OCR breach portal (August 2026). CareCloud mailed notices to over 345,000 patients on August 3, 2026, including 270,197 Texas residents.

Incident: HealthEC (population health management platform) breach
Access path: Unknown actor accessed HealthEC systems 14-23 July 2023 and copied files containing data of HealthEC's provider clients' patients; entry method not reported
Orgs reached (as reported): About 19-20 provider clients named in HealthEC's notice (HIPAA Journal summary of the notice; clients notified from 26 Oct 2023); e.g. Corewell Health and MD Valuecare
Coding notes: Notice PDFs returned 403; notice details taken via search snippets and HIPAA Journal paraphrase. Entry method, ransomware and techniques not reported. Count of affected entities rests on that secondary summary. HHS figure rose 4,452,782 to 4,656,293 to 4,786,241 (Aug 2025). Maine AG first listed 112,005 (one client only).
People or orgs exposed: 4,786,241 individuals (HHS OCR updated report, August 2025, as reported by HIPAA Journal); originally 4,452,782 (Dec 2023)
